# Roof racks and crossbars

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Mount a drop-in cargo rack and install crossbars to serve as roof racks. [t40]

Cut strut channel lengths, drill holes slightly larger than ⅜ inch, and mount crossbars with spring nuts. [t271]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Mount the drop-in cargo rack onto the factory roof rails.
2. Install Unistrut or Superstrut bars across the width of the rack to serve as crossbars.

_Procedure reported by [t40]._

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t271] [Partial]</summary>

1. Cut 40 to 48 inch lengths of strut channel (or a 6'8" length cut in half) to span the roof width.
2. Drill holes through the solid strut channel using a bit slightly larger than 3/8 inch for direct mounting.

</details>

## Parts

- Drop-in Cargo Rack: Specifically a 'Golf Cart Roof Rack' style [t40]
- [Partial] Unistrut or Superstrut bars: Used as crossbars to replace OEM ones if desired [t40]

## Specifications

- **Spring nut size and thread**: 3/8" [t271] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Strut channel ID**: 2 3/8" [t271] ([Partial] [Unverified] single report)
- **U-Bolt part number**: 3176T36 [t271] ([Partial] [Unverified] single report)

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Position the rack at a height that balances clearance underneath with stability. [t40]
- Consider mounting an awning using the ends of the Unistrut bars on one side. [t40]
- Use solid strut channel instead of slotted hole to prevent spring nuts from shifting and poking through. [t271]
- Cut 8 foot lengths in half if you need overhang for carrying a canoe. [t271]
